SPACE JUNK DIALYSIS
2025

KALPA is one of my speculative wearable interactive installations. It explores the conflict between future extra-terrestrial commercial expansion and the microscopic ecology of the human body.

In ancient Sanskrit, Kalpa signifies the lifecycle of a cosmos—an eon of creation, existence, and ultimate dissolution. Today, we accelerate our own cycle. As dead satellites ignite upon atmospheric re-entry, they are curated as a beautiful collective delusion: “artificial meteor showers.” Yet, this celestial romance cascades as a toxic heavy-metal rain—vaporized aluminum, nickel, and chromium drifting into the sacred, immediate act of our breathing.

KALPA collapses the cosmic timeline into a single, fragile inhalation.

Driven by real-time airflow sensors, this wearable bio-synthetic apparatus forces a visceral symbiosis: as the universe burns above, the fluid pumps pulse below, mimicking a kidney dialysis to filter the debris of deep-space exploration from our very bloodstream.

We are no longer just stargazers. We have become the final filters of a dying galaxy.

Are we reaching for the cosmos, or merely drowning in its ash?

407 × 468 × 230 mm
Medium
